findings.description: Test name says denials 'are recorded as unknown when the result carries no list' but the assertion is `toBeNull()`. `docs/conventions/testing.md` L11 says 'name tests by the behaviour they pin down'. Rename it, e.g. 'are recorded as null when the result carries no list'. The 'unknown' fallback is the separate per-entry `tool_name` default, which no test covers.

The cell says "the tool calls the allowlist refused". The schema `.describe()` and the review-retro sentence both say "the run's permission rules refused". `permission_denials` in the result covers any permission refusal, not only allowlist misses. Suggested wording: "the tool calls the permission rules refused".

`recordFor` is the fourth copy of the mkdtemp + execution-file + `spawnSync(tsx, review-metrics.script.ts)` harness already in `spend-split-by-model.test.ts` (`runMetrics`) and siblings; a shared `test/integration/run-metrics.ts` helper would stop the next field adding a fifth.

The 200-character cap is a bare literal in `text.slice(0, 200)` and is repeated in the schema `.describe("...cut to 200 characters.")` and the test's `toHaveLength(200)`; a named constant would keep the three in step.

priorRecords matches records by grepping the raw text for `"pr_number": N,` and never checks that the parsed `pr_number` equals N, so any free text in a record containing that string makes it a prior for PR N. Model-written finding and process-issue text already allowed this. The new `permission_denials[].input` adds another way in: a denied command quoting that string is stored as `\"pr_number\": N,`, which still contains the pattern. Adding `parsed.pr_number === Number(prNumber)` to the loop closes it.

The allowlist entry `Bash(gh api repos/*)` matches by prefix, so it also lets through write calls like `gh api repos/O/R/issues/N/comments -f body=...` or `gh api -X PUT repos/O/R/contents/...`. Those would run with the action's write token. That contradicts the "allowlist has no write verbs" guarantee in the workflow comment and `tools/review/README.md`. A pattern limited to GET, or a scoped `gh api` wrapper, would close it.
